Name: Ai (et-Tell) (העי (א-תל))
Description: Bell-shaped cisterns cut into the soft chalk rock, located beneath or near houses. One cistern was connected to two others, possibly for sedimentation, and was sealed when the house was abandoned around 3000 years ago (Iron Age I).

Name: Khirbet Raddana (חורבת רדנה)
Description: Bell-shaped cisterns cut into the soft chalk rock, located beneath or near houses. These cisterns were crucial due to the distant and small local spring, providing sufficient water for the Iron Age I inhabitants.

Name: Tel Beersheba (תל באר שבע)
Description: An ancient well located on the southeastern side of the tel. Its upper part is associated with the early layers (VI-IX) of Tel Beersheba, dating to Iron Age I (11th century BCE). The well is very deep, reaching 69m, and was likely connected to the earliest settlement.

Name: Tel Beit Shemesh (תל בית שמש)
Description: A large well, 3.3m in diameter, discovered north of the city gate. Its upper part is built with large stones. Mackenzie attributed it to the Philistine fortified city, dating its use to Iron Age I.

Name: Tel Dor (תל דור)
Description: A rectangular well cut into kurkar rock, reaching the shallow water table. It underwent three construction phases, with pottery dating its use from the late 13th to early 11th century BCE (Iron Age I). It was built with ashlar stones and protected from sea waves.

Name: Tel Gerisa (תל גריסה)
Description: An Iron Age I well built into an older Middle Bronze Age water system. It is a rectangular vertical shaft, constructed with large, roughly hewn stones, and its use is attributed to the Philistine settlement from the 11th century BCE.

Name: Tel Hazor (תל חצור)
Description: Two rock-cut aqueducts (northern and southern) were found west and southwest of the tel. They are unplastered and their early date is suggested by sherds in their fill, possibly dating to the Iron Age or even Early Bronze Age II.

Name: Tel Shiloh (תל שילה)
Description: A rock-cut and plastered cistern (Cistern 1320) found in the courtyard of an Iron Age I house (Layer V and IV).

Name: Tel Taanach (תל תענך)
Description: A cistern located beneath a courtyard of a building dated to the late 12th century BCE. It is 13.3m deep, with a built neck of 7m, and was fed by a plastered drainage channel from the courtyard.

Name: Tell es-Sa'idiyeh (תל א-סעידיה)
Description: A monumental stepped water system with 95 preserved steps, leading down to a hidden spring. It was covered to conceal it from enemies. The system includes a small semi-circular pool and a plastered underground channel, dating its initial use to the mid-12th century BCE (Iron Age I).
